headline: Revenue rose 2.5x over FY24-FY26 to Rs 106.76 cr with PAT of Rs 13.38 cr, but operating cash flow was negative in two of three years, 83.6% of revenue comes from ten customers, and the Rs 155.03 cr of identified objects imply a price of at least Rs 44.29 against Rs 17.50 in the last secondary transfers.
red_flags: Revenue Rs 41.87 cr to Rs 106.76 cr FY24-FY26 (2.5x); PAT Rs 8.63 cr to Rs 13.38 cr, down 17.1% in FY26 (p. 84)
Cumulative CFO/PAT -25.7%; receivables 211 closing days, Rs 14.10 cr outstanding 1-3 years (pp. 39, 86-87; Annex. 14)
Top-10 customers 83.58% of FY26 revenue, top-1 18.73%; Government share fell from 58.36% to 26.84% (pp. 49-50)
Related-party purchases and services Rs 14.11 cr (24.3% of purchases); related-party supplier advances Rs 8.06 cr (pp. 89-92)
Objects floor Rs 44.29 per share vs Rs 17.50 secondary price; blended fair value Rs 17.71 (Neutral)
Contracted growth: 20-year UP concession for 20 institutes and MoU for 50 AICTE labs; 30 labs already equipped (pp. 134-145)

flags: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -81.9% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause
RED: objects floor sits above blended fair value
model.reverse_dcf: The price asks the business to deliver 325.7 times its current free cash flow, in perpetuity.

reference_note: Rs 44.29 per share: the objects floor, i.e. identified objects of Rs 155.03 cr divided by the fixed fresh issue of 3.50 crore shares, before offer expenses and general corporate purposes (pp. 134-135). Not a price band. The last secondary transfers (Apr-Jun 2026) were at Rs 17.50 (p. 207).

strengths: Revenue 2.5x in two years: Rs 41.87 cr to Rs 106.76 cr FY24-26 (p. 84)
Current tax 32.0% of cumulative PBT; no contingent liabilities (p. 84; Annex. 43)
20-year concession for 20 UP institutes and MoU for 50 AICTE labs; Rs 27.74 cr already deployed (pp. 134-145)
DGCA type-certified VIRAJ drone; 162 units deployed (p. 271)
Reg 6(1) tests met: average operating profit Rs 18.38 cr (p. 459)
weaknesses: Cumulative CFO -Rs 9.82 cr against PAT Rs 38.16 cr (pp. 86-87)
Related-party costs 24.3% of FY26 purchases; advances Rs 8.06 cr (pp. 89-92)
Drone sales Rs 10.40 cr to Rs 3.40 cr; production 4 to 100 units a quarter against 600 installed capacity (pp. 50, 301)
opportunities: Issuer-commissioned report: Indian drone market Rs 2.95 lakh cr by 2030, 35% CAGR (p. 239)
AV labs to train 60,000 candidates a year from FY28 (p. 137)
Haryana incentive package Rs 58.51 cr NPV for Future Tech Park (p. 272)
NSDC co-investment agreement of 24-Jul-2026 for advanced skilling centres (p. 269)
threats: Receivable collection from authorities: Rs 14.10 cr outstanding 1-3 years (Annex. 14)
Budget and tender dependence of Government and government-funded customers (p. 50)
Rs 17.41 cr capital commitments and Rs 25.81 cr capital advances to vendors (Annex. 12, 43)
FIR 33/2025 under s. 420 IPC; director summoned (pp. 447-448)
